concerns.text: The plan specifies a 'single-sample t-test' on squared errors to compare CNN vs. Baseline. This is statistically invalid. A single-sample t-test compares a sample mean against a known constant (e.g., 0). Here, you are comparing two dependent samples (CNN errors and Baseline errors for the same images). The correct test is a 'paired t-test' (dependent samples t-test). Using a single-sample test here renders the statistical conclusion (FR-005, SC-002) methodologically unsound and likely to produce incorrect p-values.

The plan defines the sensitivity analysis threshold as 'median predicted strength' and sweeps 'around' it. However, the spec (FR-007) and success criteria (SC-003) require assessing robustness for classifying 'high strength' materials. If the threshold is the median of the *predictions*, the resulting FPR/FNR will be trivially determined by the model's own distribution (approx 50% split) rather than testing robustness against a physically meaningful or ground-truth-based threshold. The threshold source must be independent of the model's prediction distribution (e.g., ground-truth median or a fixed physical value) to avoid a tautological validation of the model's own bias.

The plan states: 'Calculate prediction confidence intervals using test set residuals'. This introduces data leakage. The test set must remain unseen until the final evaluation. Calculating residuals (errors) on the test set to derive confidence intervals for the test set predictions uses the answer to construct the uncertainty estimate. The correct methodology is to calculate residuals on the *validation* set (or a held-out calibration set) and apply that distribution to the test set predictions. Using test set residuals invalidates the independence of the test set.

The plan initializes MobileNetV2 with 'frozen ImageNet weights' and trains only the head. While computationally efficient, this assumes ImageNet features (natural images) are transferable to EBSD microstructure images (grain boundaries, crystallographic orientation maps). This is a significant domain shift. Without an ablation study comparing 'frozen backbone' vs. 'fine-tuned backbone' (even with a small learning rate), the plan cannot scientifically validate whether the model is learning microstructure features or just relying on the head to map generic textures. The current design risks a false negative (model fails because features aren't transferable) or false positive (model learns artifacts). The ablation in Phase 1 only covers augmentation, not backbone fine-tuning.
